# Ctrl + Wheel Zoom

Hold **Ctrl** (or **⌘** on macOS) and roll the mouse wheel to zoom the whole Harness Web UI.
A page-

zoom plugin for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, distributed as an ordinary
DSH **profile bundle**: no
build step, no runtime dependency, plain ESM.
## What it does
| Gesture | Result |

| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + wheel | Zooms the page around the pointer, 50%–200%, in 10% steps |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘`

+ `+` / `-` | Same from the keyboard |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `0` | Back to 100% |
| Zoom chip (bottom-rig
ht) | Appears whenever the level is not 100%: click the percentage to reset, click **Fit to width**

to fit the window |
| Settings → General | A **Page zoom** row with the host's stepper pattern and a

ow |
| Settings → General | A **Page zoom** row with the host's stepper pattern and a reset button |

The chosen level is remembered in the browser (`localStorage`), and every listener, stylesheet and
t
he applied `zoom` property are removed when the plugin is disabled or unloaded.

A gesture that another component already handled (`preventDefault()`, e.g. an embedded code editor
o
r map with its own `Ctrl`+wheel zoom) is never stolen.
## Install

Ask the Harness agent to install it, or call the plugin manager yourself with the package located
by
absolute path, a tarball, or a published name:

`install_bundle` links the package into the active profile (`$DSH_PROFILE_DIR`), adds it to the
prof

ile's bundle list, and the Harness applies it live. A page refresh picks up the browser half in
a pa
ge that was already open.

To install it by hand instead, add the package to the profile's dependencies and to
`dsh.profile.bun
dles` in `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/package.json`, then restart the Harness.

## Requirements

- A Harness Web GUI (the client half declares `platform: "web"`; it is inert without a browser).
- N

othing else: the package has no dependencies, no build output, and no install scripts. Built-in
clie
nt modules (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`) come from the shell's own module table.
## Sharing and publishing
The package is self-contained, so there are three ways to hand it to someone else.
### 1. A tarball
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Send that `.tgz`; the receiver installs it by path:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

(`pnpm pack` writes the tarball beside `package.json`. DSH's own runtime ships a pnpm, so nothing
ha
s to be installed first.)
### 2. The directory (zip / repository)

Zip this folder (or push it to a Git repository) and have the receiver install the **unpacked
direct

ory** by path — `install_bundle` accepts a directory, and a folder is enough because there is
no bui

path — `install_bundle` accepts a directory, and a folder is enough because there is
no build step.
### 3. npm (install by name for everyone)

This manifest is already publishable: `name` is the unscoped `dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom`, the row in
`cord
is.patch.yml` names the same specifier, and there is no `"private": true`.

npm no longer issues long-lived "classic" tokens — they were permanently revoked on 2025-12-09 —
and
publishing requires two-factor authentication. Pick one of the two ways through:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A token without bypass-2FA is refused with `403 ... Two-factor authentication or granular access
tok

en with bypass 2fa enabled is required to publish packages`. Verify what a token can actually do
bef
ore blaming the command:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Note npm's stated direction: bypass-2FA tokens are on a path to removal (targeted for January 2027)

in favour of staged publishing or trusted publishing, so a long-lived automated release will need
on

ed publishing or trusted publishing, so a long-lived automated release will need
one of those later.

Keep `name` in `package.json` and the `name:` line of `cordis.patch.yml` identical in every
release
— the loader resolves the row through that specifier. Bump `version` for each release.
Afterwards anyone installs it by name:

## Files
| File | Role |
| `index.js` | Host half: an empty `apply()`; the row exists so the bundle can be installed and togg

led |
| `client.js` | Browser half: wheel/keyboard gestures, zoom state, chip and settings-row regis

trations, stylesheets |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The loader patch that inserts the `ctrl-wheel-zoom` r

ow |
| `locale/{zh,en}.json` | Plugin-card title/description text; the row's own copy lives in `clie

nt.js` |
| `icon.svg` | Plugin-manager card artwork |
## How the zoom works

Zoom is CSS `zoom` on the document element. It scales layout, text and fixed overlay layers
together

exactly like the browser's own page zoom, while the app's own scroll containers keep
working — a `t

ransform: scale()` wrapper cannot scroll its oversized content, and a font-size
change would only to

scale()` wrapper cannot scroll its oversized content, and a font-size
change would only touch text.

The wheel listener is registered in the capture phase on `window`, so it sees the gesture before
the

app's scroll containers and blocks them from scrolling while `Ctrl` is held. When the viewport
itse
lf scrolls, the plugin re-anchors it so the content under the pointer stays under the pointer.

Both UI surfaces read one store instance shared with the gesture writer, so the chip, the settings
s
tepper and the wheel listener can never disagree about the current level.
